builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: From Repositories to Training Environments: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding Agents with Environment Evolution Loop
summary: RepoFactory replaces linear repository-to-environment pipelines that stop at validation with an Environment Evolution Loop that uses proxy feedback to jointly optimize validity, structural coupling, and implementation scope across 17 software domains. Adoption requires constructing and maintaining a scalable evolution loop and proxy evaluation infrastructure, with costs in pipeline complexity, compute for generating and validating 10k+ environments, and potential engineering effort to adapt to proprietary codebases; the paper does not quantify inference latency or memory overhead. Proxy signals can misalign with actual training value, evolved environments may overfit to specific repository distributions or benchmarks, and verifiable feedback mechanisms can fail on real-world production code that deviates from training domains.
rationale: The reader has constrained infrastructure and no foundation-model training capability, and this technique targets large-scale environment synthesis and model training rather than immediate production adoption on a single 24 GB GPU.
technique: Automated repository-to-verifiable-environment pipeline with evolutionary optimization

claims.statement: RepoFactory replaces linear repository-to-environment pipelines that stop at validation with an Environment Evolution Loop that uses proxy feedback to jointly optimize validity, structural coupling, and implementation scope across 17 software domains. Adoption requires constructing and maintaining a scalable evolution loop and proxy evaluation infrastructure, with costs in pipeline complexity, compute for generating and validating 10k+ environments, and potential engineering effort to adapt to proprietary codebases; the paper does not quantify inference latency or memory overhead. Proxy signals can misalign with actual training value, evolved environments may overfit to specific repository distributions or benchmarks, and verifiable feedback mechanisms can fail on real-world production code that deviates from training domains.

Training Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on 10,159 evolved environments yields +22.6 percentage points on NL2Repo-Bench and +8.5 points average across five benchmarks, versus +17.5 and +6.4 points without environment evolution; no multiplicative factor is stated.
